sections.content: How many people are "research and development (r&d) managers"?

49,900 people

were counted on the census as "research and development (r& d) managers" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Managers in this unit group organise, co-ordinate and manage resources to undertake the systematic investigation necessary for the development of new products and services, or to enhance the performance of existing products and services.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 35 to 39 years. Of the whole working population 11.5% were aged 35 to 39 years. For people working as "research and development (r& d) managers", 18% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "research and development (r& d) managers" was 16 to 19 years.

  • clinical psychologists
  • business and financial project management professionals
  • sales accounts and business development managers

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "research and development (r& d) managers" there were more men than women (56.7% compared with 43.3%).

This means "research and development (r& d) managers" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "science, research, engineering and technology professionals".

Men made up 56.7% and women made up 43.3% of "research and development (r& d) managers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "research and development (r& d) managers" included:

  • business and financial project management professionals
  • financial managers and directors
  • sales related occupations (other)

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "research and development (r& d) managers", 6.9% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (91.8% compared with 8.2%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (96.6%) than self-employed (3.4%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Lambeth, this is in the same region of London.
